## Import

### QE OK

```{r}

#QE <- vroom(here("data","APP_breakdown_history.csv"),
#            col_types = cols(
 
QEmonthly <- vroom(here("data","APP_breakdown_history.csv"))

names(QEmonthly)[1] <- paste("Year")
names(QEmonthly)[2] <- paste("Month")
names(QEmonthly)[3] <- paste("Mnet_1")
names(QEmonthly)[4] <- paste("Mnet_2")
names(QEmonthly)[5] <- paste("Mnet_3")
names(QEmonthly)[6] <- paste("Mnet_4")

# QEmonthly <- na.omit(QEmonthly)

QEmonthly <- QEmonthly|>
  mutate(Mnet_1 = as.numeric(Mnet_1),
         Mnet_2 = as.numeric(Mnet_2),
         Mnet_3 = as.numeric(Mnet_3),
         Mnet_4 = as.numeric(Mnet_4))


QEmonthly <- QEmonthly|>
  mutate(Mnet = Mnet_1+Mnet_2+Mnet_3+Mnet_4)

# QE values (final)
QE_mnet <- QEmonthly |> select(Year, Month, Mnet)


QE_mnet <- QE_mnet |>
  mutate(
    Month = stringr::str_to_title(Month),
    Month_num = match(Month, month.name),
    Month_num = ifelse(is.na(Month_num), match(Month, month.abb), Month_num),
    date_first = make_date(year = Year, month = Month_num, day = 1),
    last_day = days_in_month(date_first),
    DATE = paste0(Year,"/", Month_num, "/", last_day)
  ) |>
  select(-Month_num, -date_first, -last_day)


QE_mnet <- QE_mnet|>
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(DATE, format = "%Y/%m/%d"))

rm(QEmonthly)
```

### corp int OK

```{r}
corp_int <- vroom(here("data","corp_int.csv"))

corp_int <- corp_int |>

    str_detect(., "MIR\\.M\\.[A-Z]{2}\\."),
    str_extract(., "(?<=MIR\\.M\\.)[A-Z]{2}(?=\\.)"),

names(corp_int)[23] <- paste("U2")

corp_int <- corp_int |>

corp_int <- corp_int|>

    names_to = "Country",

```

### First join

```{r}
data <- inner_join(QE_mnet,corp_int,by=join_by(DATE)) |>
  select(DATE,Country,Mnet,int)
```

## Data loading and cleaning : other variables

Each data file downloaded from the ECB Data Portal is loaded and cleaned as follows:

We start by loading the dataset from our data folder, and computing the original number of rows and columns. We use the function spec() with the col_types() argument to preserve the date format for `DATE`, and the numeric type for variables that are incorrectly recognized as logical.

Two columns are for the date : `DATE` as a date,`TIME PERIOD` as a character. The others are the values for the twenty countries of the Euro Union. Each of these column corresponds to a full ECB series name, for example: `Financial account, Direct Investment, Net (BPS.M.N.IE.W1.S1.S1.T.N.FA.D.F5._Z.EUR._T._X.N.ALL)`. We rename each column by extracting the two letter country code from the series name, using the function ifelse.

Next, we select all columns except `TIME PERIOD` (we will use `DATE` for joining) and Hungary's values, as this country's target variable is not available. We also filter the observations from October 2014 to November 2025. 

Finally, we transform the dataset from wide format (months as rows, countries as columns) to long format (months and countries as rows), and left join to the full `data` dataset.

### Net investments

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# We load the dataset and compute the initial number of rows and columns
invest <- vroom(here("data","Net_direct_investments.csv"), 
                col_types = cols(
  DATE = col_date(format = ""),
  `TIME PERIOD` = col_character(),
  `Financial account, Direct Investment, Net (BPS.M.N.IE.W1.S1.S1.T.N.FA.D.F5._Z.EUR._T._X.N.ALL)` = col_double(),
  `Financial account, Direct Investment, Net (BPS.M.N.NL.W1.S1.S1.T.N.FA.D.F5._Z.EUR._T._X.N.ALL)` = col_double()
))
                
invest_init_col <- ncol(invest)
invest_init_row <- nrow(invest)
invest_init_na <- sum(is.na(invest))


# We rename the columns of dataset
invest <- invest |>
  rename_with(~ ifelse(
    str_detect(., "BPS\\.M\\.N\\.[A-Z]{2}\\.W1"),
    str_extract(., "(?<=BPS\\.M\\.N\\.)[A-Z]{2}(?=\\.)"),
    .
  ))

# We select the variables and filter the date
invest <- invest |>
  select(!`TIME PERIOD`) |>
  select(!HR) |> 
  filter(DATE >= as.Date("2014-10-01") & DATE <= as.Date("2025-11-30"))

# We pivot to long format
invest <- invest |>
    pivot_longer(
    cols = -DATE,
    names_to = "Country",
    values_to = "Invest"
  )
```

|                   | Before cleaning       | After cleaning      |
|-------------------|-----------------------|---------------------|
| Number of columns | `r invest_init_col`   | `r ncol(invest)`        |
| Number of rows    | `r invest_init_row` | `r nrow(invest)`        |
| Number of NAs     | `r invest_init_na`  | `r sum(is.na(invest))` |


We decided to keep a complete dataset and select all the countries except the one of Hungary, resulting in a lot of missing values even after cleaning (AT, CY, IE, NL have no time series available). We will eventually delete some missing countries for the analysis.

We then join this dataset to the full one.

```{r}
data2 <- left_join(data,invest,by=join_by(DATE,Country))
```

### Harmonised index of consumer prices (HICP)

```{r}
# We load the dataset and compute the initial number of rows and columns
HICP <- vroom(here("data","HICP.csv"),
              delim = ",") #correct the problem of delimitation

HICP_init_col <- ncol(HICP)
HICP_init_row <- nrow(HICP)
HICP_init_na <- sum(is.na(HICP))

# We rename the columns 
HICP <- HICP |>
  rename_with(~ ifelse(
    str_detect(., "ICP\\.M\\.[A-Z]{2}\\."),  
    str_extract(., "(?<=ICP\\.M\\.)[A-Z]{2}(?=\\.)"),
    .
  ))

# We select and pivot to long format
HICP <- HICP |>
  select(!`TIME PERIOD`) |>
  select(!HR) |>
  filter(DATE >= as.Date("2014-10-01") & DATE <= as.Date("2025-11-30"))

HICP <- HICP |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -DATE,
    names_to = "Country",
    values_to = "HICP"
  )

# We join to the previous dataset
data3 <- left_join(data, HICP, by=join_by(DATE,Country))
```

### ST interest rate (Euribor)

We import two short-term interest rates, common to all euro-area countries and set by the ECB, with maturities of three and six months.

We then compute the real interest rate for each country. Using the Fisher approximation, the real rate is obtained by subtracting a country's expected inflation rate from the nominal interest rate.

```{r}
ST3M_int <- vroom(here("data","Euribor_3M.csv"))

colnames(ST3M_int) <- c("DATE","TIME PERIOD","ST3M")

ST3M_int <- ST3M_int |>
  mutate(ST3M = as.numeric(ST3M))

ST3M_int <- ST3M_int |>
  mutate(
    DATE = as.Date(DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  ) |>
  filter(DATE >= as.Date("2014-10-01") & DATE <= as.Date("2025-11-30"))

ST3M_int <- ST3M_int |>
  select(DATE, ST3M)

# 6 month 

ST6M_int <- vroom(here("data","Euribor_6M.csv"))

colnames(ST6M_int) <- c("DATE","TIME PERIOD","ST6M")

ST6M_int <- ST6M_int |>
  mutate(ST6M = as.numeric(ST6M))

ST6M_int <- ST6M_int |>
  mutate(
    DATE = as.Date(DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d")
  ) |>
  filter(DATE >= as.Date("2014-10-01") & DATE <= as.Date("2025-11-30"))

ST6M_int <- ST6M_int |>
  select(DATE, ST6M)


data4 <- left_join(data3,ST3M_int,by="DATE")

data4 <- left_join(data4,ST6M_int,by="DATE")
```

### LT interest rates

As well as the columns "Date", "Time Period" and the country values, there are two aggregates of code I9 (Euro area 20 (fixed composition) as of 1 January 2023) and U2 (Euro area changing composition), hence 24 columns.

```{r}
LT10Y_int <- vroom(here("data","LT_interest_rate.csv"))

LT10Y_int <- LT10Y_int |>
  rename_with(~ ifelse(
    str_detect(., "IRS\\.M\\.[A-Z0-9]{2}\\."),
    str_extract(., "(?<=IRS\\.M\\.)[A-Z0-9]{2}(?=\\.)"),
    .
  ))

LT10Y_int <- LT10Y_int |>
  mutate(DATE = as.Date(DATE, format = "%Y-%m-%d"))

LT10Y_int <- LT10Y_int |>
  filter(DATE >= as.Date("2014-10-01") & DATE <= as.Date("2025-11-30")) 

LT10Y_int <- LT10Y_int |>
  select(DATE, AT, BE, CY, DE, EE, ES, FI, FR, GR, HR, IE, IT, LT, LU, LV, MT, NL, PT, SI, SK, U2
  ) # we don't select I9

LT10Y_int <- LT10Y_int |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -DATE,
    names_to = "Country",
    values_to = "LT10Y_int"
  )

data5 <- left_join(data4, LT10Y_int, by = join_by(DATE, Country))
```
